[abstract]
This document is an original “kitchen-sink” sample intended to exercise a wide range of AsciiDoc markup.
It intentionally includes many edge cases (nesting, continuations, spans, passthroughs, and table features).

== Footnotes

Here is an example footnote.footnote:[This is an original example footnote with no reused prose.]

You can also add an index term. indexterm:[kitchen sink example]

== Paragraphs

.Optional title
A simple paragraph with an optional title.

Paragraphs can be split across lines
and still be rendered as a single paragraph.

Paragraphs are separated by a blank line.

Another paragraph that exists mainly to verify that paragraph boundaries are respected.

.A literal paragraph
 This is a literal paragraph.
 Literal paragraphs must be indented.

.JavaScript source
[source,javascript]
----
const fact = (n) => (n <= 1 ? 1 : n * fact(n - 1));
----

Another simple paragraph after a code block.

== Notices

.Paragraph as a NOTE with optional title
NOTE: This is an example single-paragraph note.

---
TIP: Tip.

---
IMPORTANT: Important.

---
WARNING: Warning.

---
CAUTION: Caution.

.*Listing* block

Use this for: code or file listings.

.*Source* block
[source,javascript]
----
// Use this for: highlighted code listings.
function add(a, b) {
  return a + b;
}
----

.A Sidebar block
****
Use this for sidebar notes.
Sidebars can be multiple paragraphs.

Second paragraph inside a sidebar.

========

    print(f"Hello, {name}!")
----

====
Some note remarks go here.

.*A note* admonition block
[NOTE]
===============================
Use this for multi-paragraph notes.

Second paragraph in an admonition block.
===============================

---

There is a comment below.

////
// Comment block
// Use this to hide content from rendered output.
////

The comment above should not appear in output.

---

++++
<!-- Passthrough block: backend-specific markup (HTML in this case). -->
<div class="passthrough-demo">
  <p><strong>Raw HTML</strong> inside a passthrough block.</p>
  <ol>
    <li>One</li>
    <li>Two</li>
    <li>Three</li>
  </ol>
</div>
++++

---

.*Literal* block
....
Use this when indentation-based literal paragraphs conflict with list parsing.

1. This line looks like an ordered list item,
2. but in a literal block it stays literal.
....

---

.*Quote* block
[quote, "Case Notes", "Collected Observations"]
____
A carriage rolled past with a soft rattle of wheels.
The watcher paused, counted the steps, and wrote down what the sound implied.

"It narrows the options," they said, "not because it proves anything, but because it excludes what cannot be."
____

[NOTE]
.A NOTE admonition block with nested lists
=====================================================================
A paragraph at the top of an admonition block.

. First ordered item
. Second ordered item
.. Nested ordered item
.. Another nested ordered item
. Third ordered item

* A bulleted list can also appear here.
** With nesting.
=====================================================================

== Text

You can force +
a line break.

Text can be normal, _italic_, *bold*, and +mono+.

Quotes can be "double quoted" or 'single quoted'.
Quotes can be "`double curly quoted`" or '`single curly quoted`'.

Text can be normal, ^superscripted^, and ~subscripted~.

You can use backquotes for commands: `ls -al`.

+mono *bold*+ `passthru *bold*`

Path-like text: `/some/path/file.txt`, `.config`

[red]#red text# [yellow-background]#on yellow# [big]#large#
[red yellow-background big]*all bold*

Mixed and tricky markup:
n__i__**b**++m++[red]##r##

Special chars: (C) (R) (TM) -- ... -> <- => <= ¶

Escaped:
\_not italic_, +++_also not italic_+++, t\__e__st, +++t__e__st+++, +++bold+++, $$normal$$
\¶ \`not single quoted' \`\`not double quoted''
